thread:
Alex S: FYI customer Acme Support reporting: reserved GPU hours show ~120h used in last 24h but token burn and API traffic are very low. They think we're draining their committed pool.
Acme Support: We saw the spike on the reserved dashboard, but our app only made a few hundred requests. invoice line shows large reserved usage. Can you explain?
Priya R: Can you paste the pool id and account id? Also any timeframe screenshots would help.
Acme Support: account: acme-42, pool: rp-204. Screenshot attached in DM.
Morgan: Kicking off quick query against metering. Suspect warmup/heartbeat VMs counted as reserved hours.
InfraBot: alert: reserved-pool-usage-high rp-204 current=119.8h threshold=100h (1h ago)
Jon (Billing Ops): A few notes: reserved GPU hours are billed by instance-uptime, not token burn. Warmup/keepalive instances and failed warm starts can consume hours without producing tokens. Also SLA credits sometimes show separately.
Alex S: We need a reproducible audit for acme-42: list all compute instances attached to rp-204 with uptime and associated request counts for the 24h window. Morgan can you share the SQL?
Morgan: Query (short):
```
SELECT instance_id, start_ts, end_ts, SUM(requests) as requests
FROM metering.instances
WHERE pool_id='rp-204' AND start_ts >= 1971140000 AND end_ts <= 1971234567
GROUP BY instance_id, start_ts, end_ts;
```
Morgan: Ran it — three instances with long uptime (one had 24h), but request counts are 0 or 1. Looks like auto-warmup/recycler kept them alive.
Priya R: Any failed batch jobs or scheduled migrations in that timeframe for acme-42?
InfraBot: deployment-event: rp-204 host-redeploy at 1971210000 by infra-ops (auto)
Alex S: That redeploy aligns with the start of the spike. Could be warmup loop: redeploy triggers new instances which are billed while controller retries.
Jon (Billing Ops): For support, we can do two things: 1) apply a manual adjustment/credit for hours attributable to orchestration retries, 2) add a note to billing so future incidents are auto-flagged. What amount should be credited?
Acme Support: We just want the billing corrected. We don't need a full RCA in billing, but we'd like to avoid recurrence.
Morgan: Short-term mitigation: add stricter backoff for redeploy warmup + limit max simultaneous warm instances. Patch ready, can deploy to infra-relay tomorrow.
Priya R: Action items: 1) Morgan to collect full instance audit + logs for rp-204 window (ETA 2h). 2) Jon to provision provisional credit and open billing adjustment ticket (#BILL-8743). 3) Alex to notify customer with interim explanation and ETA.
Alex S: Messaging to customer: "We found orchestration-triggered warmup instances that were billed but produced minimal tokens. We're applying a provisional credit and will patch the warmup flow to prevent repeats. Will follow up with full RCA." Sending now.
Acme Support: Thanks. Please keep us posted.
Jon (Billing Ops): Credit applied provisional: 45 GPU-hours (ticket BILL-8743). Final amount subject to RCA.
Morgan: Uploaded instance audit to internal ticket (link). Key snippet: instance i-0a3f had 23.8h uptime, requests=0, started at redeploy time.
Priya R: After patch deploy I'll monitor rp-204 for abnormal keepalive patterns.
Alex S: Closing loop for now — customer notified and credited. Will reopen if billing ops needs more.
Acme Support: Appreciate the quick turnaround. :thumbsup:
Jon (Billing Ops): Leaving this in billing queue for follow-up; SLA credit will be considered if orchestration found at fault.
InfraBot: incident-note: follow-up RCA required.
Alex S: Thanks team — moving to resolved-on-support side, leaving internal tickets open.
